raw: {"bundleId":"supabase-postgres-best-practices","familyTheme":"Applied Postgres remediation tasks for SaaS systems, spanning measurable query tuning and safe multi-tenant concurrency fixes.","similarTasks":[{"category":"SQL query and indexing optimization","difficulty":"medium","goal":"Produce `answer/support_dashboard_fix.sql` that updates a seeded helpdesk database with the right query rewrites and indexes so the dashboard workload keeps the same results while avoiding sequential scans and unnecessary heap fetches.","primaryOutputFile":"answer/support_dashboard_fix.sql","skillBenefitRationale":"This task benefits directly from the Supabase Postgres guidance on missing indexes, composite indexes, partial indexes, covering indexes, and EXPLAIN-based diagnosis, which are all needed to choose the minimal high-impact fixes instead of guessing.","title":"Optimize a Slow Support Dashboard Without Changing Its Results"}],"transferTasks":[{"category":"Concurrency and multi-tenant security remediation","difficulty":"medium-hard","goal":"Produce `answer/worker_queue_patch.sql` that fixes a seeded background-job database by implementing non-blocking queue claiming, tenant-safe row-level security, and the supporting indexes needed for concurrent worker and isolation tests to pass.","primaryOutputFile":"answer/worker_queue_patch.sql","skillBenefitRationale":"This task uses a different scenario from pure query tuning and requires combining queue locking patterns such as `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, short-transaction thinking, RLS correctness and performance rules, and index design from the Supabase Postgres bundle.","title":"Stabilize a Multi-Tenant Worker Queue Under Contention"}]}
